questions.question: In which month and year did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India in January 1915 after successfully leading mass resistance against racial discrimination in South Africa through satyagraha.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi organized his first successful Satyagraha in India in 1917 at Champaran (Bihar) to support peasants against:
options: Low wages in cotton textile mills
questions.explanation: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi travelled to Champaran in Bihar to inspire peasants to struggle against the oppressive indigo plantation system (tinkathia).

questions.question: What power did the Rowlatt Act of 1919 give to the British colonial government in India?
options: Power to detain political prisoners without trial for up to two years
Power to confiscate all agricultural land without compensation
Power to ban all religious gatherings across India
Power to abolish the Indian National Congress permanently
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for up to two years.

questions.question: On which historic date did the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place in Amritsar?
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 (the festival day of Baisakhi), General Dyer blocked the exits of Jallianwala Bagh and opened fire on the peaceful gathering, killing hundreds.

questions.question: Who renounced his British Knighthood in deep anguish and protest following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his British Knighthood to express national pain and outrage against the Jallianwala Bagh atrocities.

questions.question: The Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 by two brothers named:
options: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and Liaquat Ali Khan
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and Syed Ahmed Khan
Muhammad Iqbal and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
questions.explanation: A young generation of Muslim leaders, brothers Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali (Ali brothers), formed the Khilafat Committee in Bombay in March 1919 to defend the Ottoman Khalifa's temporal powers.

questions.question: In which famous 1909 book did Mahatma Gandhi declare that British rule was established in India with the cooperation of Indians and would collapse if they refused to cooperate?
questions.explanation: In his seminal book 'Hind Swaraj' (1909), Mahatma Gandhi formulated the fundamental premise that British rule survived in India solely through Indian cooperation, and would collapse within a year of non-cooperation.

questions.question: At which Congress session in December 1920 was the Non-Cooperation programme finally ratified and adopted?
questions.explanation: At the Congress session at Nagpur in December 1920, a compromise was worked out and the Non-Cooperation programme was formally adopted.

questions.question: Who led the peasant movement in Awadh against oppressive talukdars and landlords during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: In Awadh, peasants were led by Baba Ramchandra—a sanyasi who had earlier been an indentured labourer in Fiji—demanding reduction of revenue and abolition of begar.

questions.question: In October 1920, the Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up and headed by:
options: Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra, and a few others
Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Subhas Chandra Bose and Bhagat Singh
questions.explanation: By October 1920, the Oudh Kisan Sabha was formed, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra, and a few others, setting up over 300 village branches within a month.

questions.question: Who led the militant guerrilla movement of tribal peasants in the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh in the early 1920s?
questions.explanation: In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, a militant guerrilla movement unfolded under Alluri Sitaram Raju, who claimed to have astrological powers and healing abilities.

questions.question: Under which colonial legislation were plantation workers in Assam prohibited from leaving tea gardens without permission?
questions.explanation: Under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859, tea plantation workers in Assam were not permitted to leave the tea gardens without permission, and in reality such permission was rarely granted.

questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi abruptly call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
options: Because the British government accepted all demands
Because the Indian National Congress was banned
Due to outbreak of the plague in Gujarat
Due to violent clash and burning of police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur
questions.explanation: In February 1922, a peaceful demonstration in Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) turned into a violent clash where a police station was burned and 22 policemen killed. Gandhi called off the movement because it was turning violent.

questions.question: Which leaders formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress in 1923 to argue for a return to council politics?
options: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and M.R. Jayakar
questions.explanation: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to contest legislative council elections and oppose British policies from within the councils.

questions.question: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted by all political parties upon its arrival in India in 1928?
options: It recommended dividing India into twenty provinces
It was headed by General Dyer
It did not have a single Indian member
It demanded immediate introduction of martial law
questions.explanation: The problem was that the Statutory Commission constituted under Sir John Simon did not have a single Indian member; all its members were British.

questions.question: Under whose presidency did the Lahore Congress Session in December 1929 formalize the historic demand of 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence)?
questions.explanation: In December 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore Congress formalized the demand of 'Purna Swaraj' or complete independence for India.

questions.question: From where did Mahatma Gandhi begin his historic 240-mile Salt March on 12 March 1930?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi started the historic Salt March on 12 March 1930 from his ashram at Sabarmati to the coastal town of Dandi in Gujarat with 78 trusted volunteers.

questions.question: Who was devoutly referred to as 'Frontier Gandhi' and organized the Khudai Khidmatgars in the North-West Frontier Province?
questions.explanation: Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a devout disciple of Mahatma Gandhi known as 'Frontier Gandhi', led the non-violent Khudai Khidmatgars in Peshawar and the NWFP.

questions.question: The Poona Pact of September 1932 signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resulted in:
options: Reserved seats for Depressed Classes in provincial and central legislative councils to be voted by general electorate
Separate electorates for Depressed Classes in all elections
Complete reservation of executive cabinets for Dalits
Division of the presidency into separate administrative units
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact of September 1932 gave the Depressed Classes (later known as Scheduled Castes) reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by the general electorate rather than separate electorates.

questions.question: Who painted the iconic portrait of Bharat Mata in 1905, portraying her as an ascetic, calm, composed, divine, and spiritual figure?
questions.explanation: In 1905 during the Swadeshi movement, Abanindranath Tagore painted the famous portrait of Bharat Mata, portraying her as an ascetic figure radiating serenity and spiritual grace.
